reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly demonstrates that fast moving-bed pyrolysis yields uniform, non-phase-separated nanoparticles while slower heating causes phase segregation, supporting the core kinetic-quenching premise. However, the evidence is limited to a ternary NiPdPt system and does not explicitly confirm near-simultaneous nucleation of all metals, sub-5 nm nuclei, or the generalizability to noble metal precursors with comparable kinetics.
premises: Ultra-fast heating causes near-simultaneous nucleation of all metals
Rapid nucleation kinetically locks in a uniform, stochastic elemental distribution
Kinetic quenching suppresses diffusion and prevents phase separation
Slower heating allows differential atomic mobility leading to segregation
The mechanism applies to noble metal precursors with comparable reduction kinetics
